subject: Recap & next steps — Dedicated vs hyperscaler capacity (Acme evaluation)
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Jun 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Recap & next steps — Dedicated vs hyperscaler capacity (Acme evaluation)

Jane — great to meet today, thank you for the time. Quick recap from our discovery and proposed next steps so the team has a single place to reference:

Summary of needs (from your notes):
- POC target: latency-sensitive chat + batch embedding workloads (multi-tenant)
- Expected concurrency: ~50 concurrent sessions during peak testing
- Data residency: US-only for POC, potentially EU later
- Timeline: POC start target week of Jul 6, decision end of Q3

Where Redwood Dedicated shows up vs hyperscalers (high level):
- Capacity guarantees: Dedicated = reserved GPU pools with SLA-backed throughput (we reserve capacity for your account so you don't compete in a shared pool). Hyperscalers typically offer reserved instances but not the same per-customer SLOs on model-serving throughput.
- Predictable performance: we provide per-route latency SLOs and can configure guaranteed QPS per model.
- Cost controls: committed-reserved pricing plus autoscaling/burst policies; you get planning visibility vs variable spot-like costs on public clouds.
- Ops/rollouts: unified API for canary/A-B rollouts, automatic fallback to smaller model variants if you hit capacity, and KV/prefix caching to reduce token costs.
- Compliance & private deploy: SOC2 + private VPC options for production deployments (we can share our SOC2 report).

Proposed technical tests (to validate the hyperscaler comparison):
1) Throughput & stability test: 50 concurrent streams, 8k context tokens, 72-hour sustained window. Metrics: p95 latency, error rate, throughput.
2) Failover & region test: primary region (us-west) + fallback to us-east, validate cross-region failover < 500ms additional latency for warm-cache scenarios.
3) Cost/efficiency run: run a 24-hour batch embedding job to measure tokens/embedding cost and CPU/GPU utilization.

Requested from Acme for POC prep:
- Expected model family (open or licensed) and average sequence lengths
- Representative prompt set for latency-sensitive flows
- Any egress/data residency constraints

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-capacity-compare.pdf (high-level feature/ops comparison), MAP-acme-proposed-mop.xlsx (proposed mutual action plan).

Next steps / proposed dates:
- Tech deep dive with Laura (our SE) and your SRE: Tue, Jun 22 or Wed, Jun 23 (30–45m)
- Finalize POC scope & provisioning by Jun 30

If you want, I can also provide a ballpark committed capacity quote (monthly) so you can triage vs hyperscaler reserved pricing — happy to do that after the tech deep dive.

Thanks again — I’ll loop in Laura and Camila on timing.

Best,
Markus Klein
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

Thanks Markus — this is helpful. A couple quick clarifying questions before we lock in the deep dive:

1) Capacity guarantees: can you be specific about how you map "reserved GPU pools" to concrete instance types? For example, can you guarantee A10G-equivalent or A100-equivalent GPUs for the POC, or is it an abstract compute unit?

2) Pricing: can you give a ballpark monthly committed price for the typical POC size? Our procurement asks for rough estimates upfront when evaluating hyperscaler reserved instances.

3) Data residency & egress: our security team cares about where inference logs and cached data live. Does Redwood keep any cached prompts/kv outside the VPC for Dedicated? Any egress charges we should factor in?

We attached a short doc with our POC requirements (acme-poc-reqs.docx). Our tentative POC start is Jul 6 — would like to have provisioning and a basic runbook before then.

Happy to run the Tue/Wed window for the deep dive; Tue 11am PT works for me.

Subject: Re: Recap & next steps — Dedicated vs hyperscaler capacity (Acme evaluation)

Jane — thanks for the follow-ups, answers below inline:

1) Reserved GPU mapping: we provision reserved GPU pools and can map them to equivalent GPU families for sizing. For POCs we typically allocate A10G-equivalent for cost-efficient throughput tests and A100-equivalent for high-performance model runs. The exact mapping depends on model (fp16 vs int8) and sequence length; Laura (cc'd) can propose a concrete mapping after reviewing your representative prompt set.

2) Ballpark pricing: for committed/reserved single-tenant capacity, customers typically see ranges depending on GPU class and support level. For a 4-GPU equivalent reserved pool (A10G-equivalent) the ballpark is in the mid $k per GPU per month range; A100-equivalent is higher. We can produce a firm quote once we agree on POC sizing and run duration (e.g., 72-hour sustained throughput vs 30-day reserved).

3) Data residency & caching: for Redwood Dedicated the KV/prefix cache lives in the customer VPC/tenant network — we do not retain cached prompt state outside your VPC for Dedicated. Logs and audit trails can be configured to forward to your logging endpoint or retained in our control plane depending on the Private vs Dedicated model you choose. Egress behavior follows standard cloud egress — if you run in your VPC the network egress is subject to your cloud billing; for Hosted we can provide estimates. Our SOC2 report is here: https://redwood.com/trust/soc2-report.pdf

Action items we can take this week:
- Laura to lead the technical sizing and provide an exact GPU mapping + POC acceptance criteria (Laura: can you propose config by EOD Mon?)
- We’ll provision a 72-hour throughput test (4 x A10G-equivalent) as a starter and measure p95/p99 and error rate.
- Draft a provisional committed pricing worksheet for the 4-GPU-equivalent pool for 1-month and 6-month terms.

I’ll hold Tue Jun 22 11am PT for the technical deep dive. Laura/Camila — can you join?

Thanks,
Markus

Markus / Camila — quick internal note ahead of the Tue deep dive:

- I reviewed Acme's POC doc (thanks Jane). For the 50 concurrent streams @ 8k context we should start with 4 x A10G-equivalent GPUs reserved for a 72-hour throughput run. If they want to stress larger models (70B+), we'll propose a second window with 2 x A100-equivalents for latency testing.
- Acceptance criteria suggestions: p95 < 250ms for short-chat ops, <1% error rate, KV cache hit rate > 60% on prefix-heavy prompts.
- Ops plan: we will pre-provision the reserved pool in us-west, configure routing policy to route traffic to the reserved pool first, and enable burst to hosted if they want elasticity for spike scenarios (billing notes required).
- I'll prepare the GPU mapping table and the provisioning runbook by EOD Mon and attach it to the shared HubSpot deal record.

One ask for Markus: if procurement asks for a firm monthly committed price today, I'll include a conservative estimate for the 4 x A10G-equivalent pool (with standard enterprise support) but flag that the final quote depends on model mix and run length.
